review_reference: NOT SIGNED. 0124 (recorded allergies and allergy-warning acknowledgements), the EHR clinical-safety lane's migration number. reviewed_by stays empty until the owner reads this declaration and signs it here; nothing in this branch signs it.
evidence: Single migration 0124_recorded_allergies.sql. WHAT IT DOES: two new tables, nothing else. (1) ehr.recorded_allergies: an allergy a clinician recorded for a patient at a facility (substance 1-200 trimmed characters without control characters, reaction 1-500 or null, severity mild/moderate/severe/unknown, created_by and created_by_membership_id bound to the facility by the membership foreign key), status active or entered_in_error (who, when, reason 3-500; all three exactly when entered_in_error). ehr.guard_recorded_allergy_update (new, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, no grant) allows exactly one change, active to entered_in_error by the acting account, and stamps entered_in_error_at; 0004's ehr.capture_record_version versions the insert and the marking (the marking needs app.change_reason, the entered-in-error reason); platform.reject_mutation refuses DELETE. (2) ehr.prescription_allergy_acknowledgements: append-only, one or more per prescription, each with its stage (create, activate, resume or send: Activate, Resume and sending a draft to another facility check the allergies again), indexed on prescription_id, the prescriber's reason 10-500 trimmed characters, the patient's own terms that matched (normalized, text[] default '{}', at most 50, no null), the ids of the recorded allergies that matched and whether the patient-reported allergies matched (at least one of the two); foreign key (prescription_id, patient_id, facility_id) to ehr.prescriptions; 0005's ehr.validate_append_only_clinical_actor checks attribution; platform.reject_mutation refuses UPDATE and DELETE. RLS forced on both: recorded allergies read under ehr.imported_record_read_context(patient_id) (patient-self, or a clinician with read access to the patient at the current facility, as 0094's patient-reported profile: an allergy follows the patient to every facility the patient gave access to), inserted (status active only) and updated under ehr.context_allows(patient_id, facility_id, 'write_records') (the recording facility only); acknowledgements read and inserted at their own facility (read_records, write_records). Grants (migration and runtime-grants.sql alike): SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on ehr.recorded_allergies and SELECT, INSERT on ehr.prescription_allergy_acknowledgements to hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; none to PUBLIC; no DELETE. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000, nothing applied): the tables and functions referred to exist ('0124: 0001-0094 must be applied first'); neither table nor the guard function exists ('0124: already applied'). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: new objects only; no existing table, column, constraint, policy, function, trigger or grant changes; today's services never read the new tables. SERVICE ORDER: the ehr-api that ships with 0124 checks allergies at prescription create, Activate, Resume and send of a draft, and refuses a match without an allergyAcknowledgement carrying the current warningToken (409 ALLERGY_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_REQUIRED); the website that sends the acknowledgement (health, claude/ehr-allergies-web) must be live first. PROVED on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster (created for this check, not a shared or real database): FRESH install of 0001-0108 and 0124 before the role bootstrap, bootstrap passes; UPGRADE: 0001-0108 applied and bootstrapped with the base runtime-grants.sql, then plan shows 1 pending (0124 with this sha256), apply, bootstrap with the new runtime-grants.sql passes; applying the file again answers '0124: already applied'. services/ehr-api/test/database/recorded-allergies.integration.sql passes on both databases (privileges, forced RLS, recording, attribution, invalid values, read access across facilities, purpose, marking only at the recording facility with a reason and only once, no delete, acknowledgements append-only and per facility, versions); all 82 existing database suites (database/tests and test/database) pass on the fresh database with 0124 applied. RE-CHECKED after the reviews of PR 218 (stage column replacing unique (prescription_id), index on prescription_id, acknowledgement reason 10-500, patient_reported_terms): on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster, a FRESH install of every migration with the role bootstrap passes, and recorded-allergies.integration.sql and all 84 database suites pass.
